name: Jeremiah
overview: Jeremiah was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted as the fifth among the Gadites who came to David at Ziklag. His arrival at David's location is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:1 and 12:10. This identification highlights his role among the Gadite warriors who joined David during his rise to kingship.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeremiah means 'YHWH loosens [the womb],' 'YHWH lifts up,' or possibly 'YHWH shoots, establishes,' reflecting a connection to God's actions. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:10, was not given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning related to God's intervention and support.
familyAndRelationships: Jeremiah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Gad, situating him within this tribe. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him beyond what is noted in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Jeremiah's mention as part of the Gadite contingent joining David situates him within the broader biblical narrative of David's consolidation of power. Though distinct from the prophet Jeremiah, this Gadite Jeremiah exemplifies faithful support for God's chosen king. His presence at Ziklag during David's early reign connects him to the unfolding story of Israel's monarchy and God's providential guidance in establishing David's kingdom.

keyEvents.event: Called by God as a youth
